about: page 1 $8C00-$8FFF: the AT-ST's animated legs, the laser hit tests on an AT-ST and its destruction, the init of the gun shot records, and the routines that make a TIE fighter, an AT-AT and an AT-ST fire a shot

P1:8C0D.name: atst_leg_part0
P1:8C0D.desc: first of the four parts of one AT-ST leg. X points at the leg record (track number, hip x word, hip y word) and M_X0, M_Y0 hold the hip offset. sets M_Z0 to -50, has page 0 P0_93B4 interpolate keyframe track (leg's track number + 0) for the current walk frame, and passes the four points of atst_leg_pts0 through atst_leg_points

P1:8C22.name: atst_leg_part1
P1:8C22.desc: second part of an AT-ST leg, as atst_leg_part0: M_Z0 -50, keyframe track + 1, the four points of atst_leg_pts1

P1:8C39.name: atst_leg_part2
P1:8C39.desc: third part of an AT-ST leg, as atst_leg_part0: M_Z0 -716, keyframe track + 2, the four points of atst_leg_pts2

P1:8C50.name: atst_leg_part3
P1:8C50.desc: fourth and lowest part of an AT-ST leg, as atst_leg_part0: M_Z0 -1024, keyframe track + 3, the four points of atst_leg_pts3, then two more points stepped from the last one by (128, 37, -50) and (0, -37, 0). with them the leg has its 18 perspected points

P1:8D03.name: atst_leg_points
P1:8D03.desc: adds the animation offset anim_dx, anim_dy, anim_dz to the point in M_X0, M_Y0, M_Z0, then four times adds the next (dx, dy, dz) step from the table at U to it and has bank 1 (L60DE) transform and perspect the point into the next entry of BJ_PNT. U is left after the table, X is kept

P1:8D44.name: cursor_oct_dist
P1:8D44.desc: octagon distance from the laser cursor LZ_CX, LZ_CY to the perspected point at X (x word, y word): the larger of max(dx, dy) and 9/16 of dx + dy, less 10 and not below 0, returned in D. the same arithmetic as the octagon tests of Star Wars' VWGUN and S2VW. uses tmp_scal and $4803

P1:8D83.name: atst_body_hit
P1:8D83.desc: laser test on the body of the AT-ST head just perspected (object $11), called while it is drawn with its view distance in M_XT. does nothing if a nearer hit is already in atst_hit_d. otherwise turns a radius of 110 into screen units at that distance and, if the cursor is within it of perspected point 16 or 17 (the two points on the head's centre line), records the distance in atst_hit_d and clears atst_hit_rec: the shot stops on the armour and kills nothing

P1:8DD6.name: atst_window_hit
P1:8DD6.desc: laser test on the front window of the AT-ST head, U = the AT-ST record, view distance in M_XT. if no nearer hit is recorded and the cursor is inside the rectangle spanned by perspected points 12 to 15 of the head (the four corners of the window), stores U in atst_hit_rec and the distance in atst_hit_d: this AT-ST is the one the laser will destroy

P1:8E33.name: atst_killed
P1:8E33.desc: the laser has hit an AT-ST window: jumped to through the maze from page 3 P3_980B with the record in atst_hit_rec. puts the AT-ST's universe position in M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT and starts the three-piece explosion there (bank 1 KE718 through L61A4), places the record anew or frees it (atst_place), scores 50 points while bonus_left is not zero and 500 after, sends the explosion sound and counts the kill in kill_count (50 at most). the kill that brings bonus_left to zero also scores the walker quota bonus, awards the Jedi letter (P1_9573) and bumps quota_walker

P1:8E99.name: atst_place
P1:8E99.desc: U = an AT-ST record. if the spawn count w2_spawn_a is zero or negative the record is freed (bytes 0 and 1 cleared). otherwise the record is made a fresh AT-ST: status $29 (the coordinate flag $40 kept), flags cleared, and a new place - one of x and y, chosen at random, gets $8000 added and the other a random value from -$4000 to $3FFF. an AT-ST that was not on screen is first put at the player's position, so it starts half the universe away. called for a free record by the AT-ST mover P1_86E1 and after a kill

P1:8EFC.name: gun_init
P1:8EFC.desc: the last part of Star Wars' IPGEN (the IPGEN_40 loop), called from init_general in bank 0: gives each of the six gun shot records from GUN to BJBIC its 8-byte block in math RAM from M_GN, its BIC from MS_GNBC, and clears its type so that it is free

P1:8F16.name: tie_fire
P1:8F16.desc: makes a TIE fighter fire a shot: X = the alien record, carry set on return if a shot was started. called from page 3 CPUAL and from man_tie_fire in bank 0. it first runs the slapstic's alternate sequence for page 3, so that the page select on the way back through the maze, which names page 1, selects page 3, the caller's page. in the training manual the shot is started at once in the first gun record, otherwise tie_fire_try decides. close copies: atat_fire, atst_fire and P1_9063

P1:8F32.name: tie_fire_try
P1:8F32.desc: U = the alien record. takes the entry of the shot table P1_90E4 for fire_level (17 entries of 4 bytes, the level halved during 16 frames of every 64): byte 0 becomes the alien's reload time (byte 4 of its record), no shot is fired unless a random byte is above byte 1, and the word is the highest gun record that may be used. looks for a free record from there down (P1_90D2, which returns to this routine's caller with carry clear if there is none) and falls into tie_shot_start. returns carry clear when it does not fire

P1:8F5A.name: tie_shot_start
P1:8F5A.desc: X = a free gun record, U = the alien record. starts a TIE fighter shot: life timer $40, type 1, kind 1, aim offsets from P1_9168, and the shot's point in math RAM set to the alien's position (MS_TX, MS_TY, MS_TZ of its block) less the player's. sends sound aud_cmd_3d and returns carry set

P1:8F8B.name: atat_fire
P1:8F8B.desc: makes an AT-AT fire a shot: U = the AT-AT record, carry set on return if a shot was started. called from page 0 P0_8B72 and from man_atat_fire in bank 0. it first runs the slapstic's alternate sequence for page 0, so that the page select on the way back through the maze, which names page 1, selects page 0, the caller's page. in the training manual the shot is started at once in the first gun record, otherwise atat_fire_try decides. a close copy of tie_fire

P1:8FA5.name: atat_fire_try
P1:8FA5.desc: U = the AT-AT record. as tie_fire_try without the halving of the level: the shot table entry for fire_level gives the reload time (byte 3 of the record), the random threshold and the highest gun record to use. falls into atat_shot_start when a record is free, returns carry clear when it does not fire

P1:8FC5.name: atat_shot_start
P1:8FC5.desc: X = a free gun record. starts an AT-AT shot: life timer $70, type $41, kind 2, aim offsets from P1_9168, and the shot's point in math RAM set to the muzzle position the caller left in M_XT2, M_YT2, M_ZT2 less the player's position. sends sound aud_cmd_41 and returns carry set

P1:8FF7.name: atst_fire
P1:8FF7.desc: makes an AT-ST fire a shot: U = the AT-ST record, carry set on return if a shot was started. called from P1_8B52 on this page and from man_atst_fire in bank 0. it runs the slapstic's alternate sequence for page 1, which the maze's page select names anyway, so this copy only keeps the pattern of tie_fire and atat_fire. in the training manual the shot is started at once in the first gun record (P1_9031), otherwise P1_9011 decides from the shot table

4C11.name: atst_hit_d
4C11.desc: word: view distance of the nearest AT-ST the laser cursor is on in this frame, written by atst_body_hit and atst_window_hit while the AT-STs are drawn. the laser start on page 3 (P3_95CC) sets the high byte to $FF for none, and page 3 P3_97CB compares it with the distances of the other things under the cursor and takes the nearest

4C13.name: atst_hit_rec
4C13.desc: word, goes with atst_hit_d: the record of the AT-ST whose front window the cursor is on, which atst_killed then destroys, or 0 when the nearest hit was on the body and the shot only stops there

4C8B.name: anim_frame
4C8B.desc: frame counter of the walk cycle being drawn: loaded from the walker's record before its legs are drawn, read by the keyframe interpolation page 0 P0_93B4, which clears it when the cycle wraps, and stored back in the record afterwards (byte 14 of an AT-ST record)

4C8C.name: anim_dx
4C8C.desc: word: x offset of the leg part being drawn, interpolated by page 0 P0_93B4 from the part's keyframe track for anim_frame. atst_leg_points and the AT-AT code of page 0 add it to M_X0

4C8E.name: anim_dy
4C8E.desc: word: y offset of the leg part being drawn, as anim_dx

4C90.name: anim_dz
4C90.desc: word: z offset of the leg part being drawn, as anim_dx

5098.name: s1_tx
5098.desc: MS_TX+M_S1 written as a bare address: the player's universe x position, word. the slapstic pages add it to or subtract it from an object's x to change between universe and player-relative coordinates

questions: P1:8DA4-8DAA carry three comments of Star Wars' CLBLZ (MISNAMED--DELTA X, GET THE FRACTION OF LINE, GEN %*DY,%*DX) because the three instructions match. here they load a radius and the reciprocal of a distance, so they are listed in sw_drop_comments with new comments

P1:8C00-8C0B is the tail of P1_8BC3 (draws one AT-ST leg), whose header is in the chunk before this one. the names atst_leg_part0-3 assume that routine is the leg draw: it resets the point pointer (L60CC), calls the four parts and draws object $13

P1:8FC9 gun record byte 3 is set to $41 for AT-AT and AT-ST shots and to $01 for TIE fighter and probot shots. bit 0 marks the record as used and P1_91A6 uses bits $30 for the dying shot, but nothing in this range shows what bit $40 is for

P1:8E99 status $29 written to byte 0 of an AT-ST record: bit $20 is tested before firing (P1_8B4A) and bit $40 is the universe-coordinates flag, the meaning of bits $08 and $01 is not shown in this range

P1:8F66 P1_9168 gives the shot random aim offsets (bytes 6, 7 of the gun record) when a 5 bit random number is below fire_level and zero offsets otherwise. the routine is in the next chunk, the comments here only call them aim offsets
P1:8EF2 gun_move_tab: P1_9185 indexes it with twice the shot kind and, for a kind of 5 or more, with B = 1, an odd offset into the table - that looks like a slip in the original (out of this range)

P1:90E4 (next chunk, used by tie_fire_try, atat_fire_try and P1_9011): the shot table is 17 entries of 4 bytes, $90E4-$9127, followed by the probot table P1_9128 of 16 entries to $9167. the listing shows part of both as code (P1_90FD 'no caller found', P1_9148-P1_9165): those bytes are data
4C8B-4C90 and 5098 are also used by pages 0, 2 and 3: the names anim_frame, anim_dx/dy/dz and s1_tx were chosen here and may need reconciling with the chunks of those pages
$4803 appears bare in cursor_oct_dist (P1:8D63, 8D73, 8D78) though it has Atari's temp names (TMPOCT, TMPSIZ): no new name given
